title: Who Owns the Voice in Your Head?
gist: McLeod argues the AI race is moving to the ear: OpenAI is buying hardware (io, about $6.5B) to build a persistent companion, Apple owns the earbud but rents its AI models, and current earbud silicon (NPUs, 8.3MB SRAM) runs only small cleanup models. He contends the binding constraint is memory, not TOPS, so the winning design will be distributed between ear and phone with on-die memory next to compute.

insights.claim: OpenAI paid about $6.5 billion for io, the hardware startup founded by former Apple design chief Jony Ive, and supply-chain reports describe its first product, code-named Sweet Pea, as an AI earbud built around a custom 2nm chip.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: OpenAI is vertically integrating into wearable hardware, relevant for leading-edge foundry demand and device competition.
insights.locator: A year later OpenAI paid about

insights.claim: OpenAI's strategy of building a persistent AI companion never changed despite the retreat over the Sky voice; the author reads Altman's one-word 'her' post as the company's most candid product announcement.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Reads OpenAI's hardware push as a deliberate, consistent product vision.
insights.quote: That was the retreat. The strategy never moved.

insights.claim: OpenAI pulled the Sky voice after Scarlett Johansson said she had declined an invitation to voice ChatGPT and her lawyers sent two letters; Altman said the voice belonged to another actress.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Voice likeness and IP disputes are a legal risk for voice AI products.
insights.locator: A week later Johansson released a statement

insights.claim: A competitive map: OpenAI wants to own the mind and is buying a body, Google has a mind, phone and earbud but has not assembled them, Apple owns the ear and rents the mind, and Meta put sound in open speakers rather than a camera-plus-assistant earbud.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Frames positioning of the four platform players in ambient AI wearables.

insights.claim: Apple owns the most widely worn computer in the ear yet borrows its mind: after delaying personal Siri in March 2025, it turned to Google for server-tier models in January, and the rebuilt Siri shipped with iOS 27 on that foundation.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Apple's dependence on Google for foundation models weakens its AI control and pricing leverage.
insights.quote: Apple owns the most widely worn computer in the ear and borrows the mind it was meant to hold.
insights.locator: Apple owns the ear and rents the mind

insights.claim: Apple's AI chief John Giannandrea announced retirement in December and foundation model responsibility passed to Amar Subramanya, previously engineering lead on Google's Gemini assistant.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Leadership change signals Apple's AI reset and talent sourcing from Google.
insights.locator: Apple, of course, tried to build Samantha first.

insights.claim: In China, regulators approved Apple Intelligence in July with Alibaba's Qwen and Baidu supplying the models.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Chinese AI models gain access to Apple's China installed base.

insights.claim: Unlike its past bridges to Google Maps and Intel processors, Apple's reliance on Google AI models comes without a replacement team in place because the team left.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: The dependency may be longer-lived than prior Apple vendor bridges.
insights.quote: Those bridges ended because Apple had a replacement team in place. This time the team left.

insights.claim: Apple's on-device work is better than its reputation, but it aimed the Neural Engine at features such as photos, Face ID and translation, never at a persistent self.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Apple's edge AI is feature-oriented rather than aimed at a persistent agent.
insights.locator: None of this means Apple's on-device work is weak

insights.claim: AirPods Pro 3 run on the H2 chip introduced in 2022, which applies machine learning to reduce loud intermittent noise 48,000 times a second; a new infrared heart-rate sensor pulses 256 times a second.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Shows continuous small-model inference in the ear already ships at scale.
insights.locator: The earpiece itself is no longer science fiction

insights.claim: Bestechnic's BES2800 in Samsung's Galaxy Buds3 has dual Cortex-M55 cores, a dual-core NPU, a HiFi 4 DSP and 8.3MB of SRAM, and Qualcomm's S7 Pro lists a 64-GOPS neural engine.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Benchmarks the compute and memory ceiling of today's best earbud chips.

insights.claim: In every shipping AI earbud the earbud handles sound while the 'mind' sits one or two hops away on the phone or in the cloud, making current devices Siri with better microphones.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: No current product is a true on-ear AI agent, leaving room for new architectures.
insights.quote: A device that waits to be asked and then forwards the question elsewhere is Siri with better microphones.

insights.claim: Shokz's OpenFit 2 AI sold in China from August at 1,398 yuan (about $195), sends recorded conversations via the phone to Alibaba's Qwen, and the bundled three-month AI subscription indicates the model lives in Alibaba's data centers.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Subscription-bundled cloud AI is one business model for AI earbuds.

insights.claim: Camera earbuds are already shipping in China and reports have Apple preparing camera AirPods, likely for 2027.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Vision-enabled earbuds would raise on-device compute and memory needs.

insights.claim: A companion that listens, remembers and speaks while noise cancellation and heart-rate sensing keep running is a set of concurrent processes that needs an operating system, which most earbuds, running firmware, lack.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: An OS layer for earbuds is an unfilled platform opportunity.
insights.quote: Samantha is also a software problem.

insights.claim: Sonical's CosmOS is an open operating system for the ear with a hardware abstraction layer so apps can move across processors and from cloud to phone to earbud, while Bragi licenses a turnkey platform that powers Skullcandy and licenses Bose noise cancellation.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Names early platform entrants challenging closed firmware in earbuds.
insights.locator: Two companies are trying to change that.

insights.claim: Sonical founder Gary Spittle expects an earbud app ecosystem like the smartphone, with multiple resident AI agents and the cloud called only for specific tasks, and argues the resulting category will make today's Bluetooth earbud market look tiny.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: An app-store dynamic in the ear would shift value from hardware to software and chips.
insights.quote: The same is about to happen with the ear

insights.claim: Spittle says it needs a new class of processor built AI-first with Bluetooth as just a data pipe, not Bluetooth chips with a couple of extra megabytes of RAM.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Implies a new silicon category for AI earbuds.

themes.theme: Memory as the binding silicon constraint

insights.claim: An NPU is built for bursts while a persistent companion is continuous, so the binding constraint for ear AI is memory rather than arithmetic.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Favors memory-centric design over peak TOPS in edge AI silicon.
insights.quote: The binding constraint is memory, not arithmetic.

insights.claim: The best earbud SoC holds 8.3MB of SRAM while a model that can converse holds hundreds of megabytes even when compressed, and every generated token drags those weights through the memory system.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Quantifies the memory gap that blocks on-ear conversational models.

insights.claim: Anker and CIX claim their Thus A1 reaches 5 GFLOPS versus roughly 30 MFLOPS for a conventional Bluetooth audio chip, and ByteDance's Doubao earbuds carry two 128-megabit flash parts per bud versus the typical single 32- or 64-megabit part.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Chinese earbud makers are raising compute and memory content per unit.

insights.claim: Silicon that wins ear AI will sustain throughput per milliwatt with memory next to compute, favoring vector engines streaming data continuously and dense on-die memory over another burst accelerator bolted onto a Bluetooth chip.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Points to a design winner profile for edge-AI chip vendors.

insights.claim: The companion will be distributed: the ear keeps the always-on listening, short-term state and decision to speak, while a phone or pendant holds the large model and camera over a link fast enough that the seam is not heard.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Architecture implies demand for low-latency ear-to-phone links alongside phone-class compute.

insights.claim: An October survey by a Chinese trade outlet identified two earbud AI design paths: an NPU inside the audio SoC, or a Bluetooth chip paired with a separate AI audio chip.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Two competing architectures create separate chip-vendor opportunities.
insights.locator: The earbud chip makers see the opening.
